{
  "domain": "conversational German",
  "progress": "with_people",
  "approachNotes": "Duolingo gave you words but not the reflexes for live conversation — that's normal, apps train recognition, not production. The shift now is to speak full sentences out loud, even badly, and to get used to not understanding everything at a dinner table. Focus on high-frequency phrases for family talk — opinions, reactions, questions — over vocabulary breadth. Skip grammar deep-dives for now; you'll absorb cases faster from patterns you actually use.",
  "practice": "Speak answers aloud to real questions (how was your week, what do you think) in short German sentences, then try one with family in Munich.",
  "goodLooksLike": [
    "Answers a question in German without switching to English mid-sentence",
    "Asks a follow-up question instead of just responding and stopping",
    "Recovers from a wrong word by rephrasing, not freezing"
  ],
  "pitfalls": [
    "Mistaking recognizing words on a screen for being able to produce them aloud",
    "Over-focusing on perfect grammar before building basic conversational flow",
    "Avoiding speaking until 'ready,' which never arrives without practice"
  ],
  "progressionPrinciples": [
    "Prioritize spoken survival phrases for family settings over textbook vocabulary lists",
    "Introduce grammar only once a pattern already in use needs explaining",
    "Interleave listening comprehension with speaking so both grow at the dinner table"
  ]
}
